items.title: 63475_Arnett Cobb oral history interview
items.q: I had problems in '75 with my present wife, and she walked off and left me on October the 6th

ctx.x: Told you about the Carnegie Hall situation, the Ralph Cooper situation and blah, blah, blah and about my mother. You know, after my wife died, I brought my mother out there with me, and she took care of me. But she was a woman of great understanding. And anytime I'd get depressed or have any problem, I could go to her and talk to her, and she'd always have something good to say. She was clean in thought and in heart, and never give you the wrong advice.

And, of course, I had problems in '75 with my present wife, and she walked off and left me on October the 6th, and then, of course, my mother thought everything was upset. But we was having -- lot of it was my fault. I'm drinking. I raise hell, you know, and this sort of a thing,

and she just walked because she don't like no arguments and -- can't stand it, you know. And my mother thought everything was straight and everything, so by the same token, she took sick and we were still good friends and everything. She come home and she helped me put my mother in the hospital on November 15th, got the insurance straight for her.
